audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicts its own prose: win[4]/phases[4].side give Level 6 to Ryze while phases[4].why, mid and spikes[1].text all describe Perfect Execution as Akali's kill button there; win[6]/phases[6].side give 2+ items to Akali while whys[6], late and spikes[3].text all say Ryze out-scales.
audit.why: Perfect Execution is a 675-range two-part dash whose recast executes on missing health, and it lands at 6 against a champion with no defensive ability in his kit — Arcane Mastery is mana-and-damage scaling, Rune Prison is offensive, Realm Warp is a portal. Level 6 belongs to Akali. Conversely Overload resets off every other basic ability cast, so at 2+ items Ryze's rotation speed and mana-scaled damage beat a single-target burst. The chart as written tells a player to hold their ultimate at 6 and to force fights at 2 items — exactly backwards.
audit.corrected: Level 6 flipped to Akali (7/10), 2+ items flipped to Ryze (4/10), in both win[] and phases[].side, with the whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places credit Ryze with a 'passive shield' — spikes[3].text, wants.foe[1], wants.you[0] and mid ('before his shield procs', 'before his shield and Overload can stabilize').
audit.why: Riot's text for Arcane Mastery is: spells deal extra damage based on Bonus Mana, and he gains a percentage increase to maximum Mana based on Ability Power. There is no shield anywhere in Ryze's kit. This matters for an assassin: a player told to burn burst forcing out a shield will mistime the execute window, when in fact nothing absorbs the recast of Perfect Execution. His real spike is mana-into-damage growth, which is why the late game and not a shield is the problem.
audit.corrected: Every shield reference replaced with Arcane Mastery's mana-to-damage scaling; the execute cue now says nothing absorbs it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions are absent. Rune Prison is described as a root unconditionally; Twilight Shroud is said to make her 'untargetable' so the root 'drops'; Realm Warp is described as teleporting his team onto you 'anywhere' / 'across the map'.
audit.why: Riot's Rune Prison text: it damages and slows the target, and only roots 'if the target has Flux on it'. So Spell Flux must land first — both are 615-range casts, which makes the lane a range fight. Riot's Twilight Shroud text: inside it Akali is 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks' — Rune Prison is a targeted cast, so it cannot be aimed at her at all rather than being shed after the fact; Shroud is 20/19/18/17/16s against a 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s Rune Prison, which is the scheduling the entry never gives. Realm Warp is 3000 range on 180/160/140s and teleports allies standing near the portal — a flank, not a global.
audit.corrected: Rune Prison's Flux condition and 615 range stated; Shroud's unselectability stated against a targeted cast with the 20s rank-1 cooldown; Realm Warp given its 3000 range and 140s late cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ryze.json (W, E, R descriptions and cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers appear anywhere in the entry.
audit.why: Rune Prison at 11s rank 1 versus Twilight Shroud at 20s means you do not get a Shroud for every root — the blanket 'Shroud his Rune Prison' is true roughly every other cast. Naming both numbers turns the advice into a schedule.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 numbers added to mid and whys[3].

The upside is he is squishy and immobile, so just survive to level 4-6 with enough health to commit your all-in.

At 6, make him spend Spell Flux, E-flip in and chain both casts of Perfect Execution; the second cast executes on missing health and he has no shield to eat it — Arcane Mastery is mana and damage only.
